meta.homeDescription: International symposium on the dispersal and restitution of Canarian archaeological heritage. November 12–13, 2026, TEA, Santa Cruz de Tenerife.

hero.headline: A view from the Canary Islands on the dispersal and restitution of archaeological legacies
hero.description: Part of the archaeological heritage of the Canary Islands is now held outside the archipelago. On 12 and 13 November, Tenerife will bring together museum professionals and specialists from Europe, Africa and the Americas to trace the histories of these collections and discuss the relationships that can be built today with the places from which they came.

sobreEncuentro.parrafo1: From the eighteenth century onwards, archaeological objects and Indigenous human remains from the Canary Islands entered collections in mainland Spain and abroad. Some of these histories are well known; others are only beginning to be reconstructed.
sobreEncuentro.parrafo2: Diásporas Patrimoniales grows out of the work developed by the Government of the Canary Islands through the Legado Canario Disperso programme. The symposium will bring together professionals responsible for Canarian collections abroad, specialists involved in restitution processes, and institutions reassessing the histories of their own collections.
sobreEncuentro.parrafo3: The meeting will conclude with the Santa Cruz de Tenerife Declaration, conceived as a starting point for continuing these conversations beyond November.

inscripcion.parrafo: The academic sessions will take place in person and require advance registration, subject to venue capacity. You may register for either day or for both. A confirmation email will be sent once the form has been completed.
inscripcion.ambosDiasDescripcion: One registration gives you access to both days of the symposium.
inscripcion.yaInscritoParcial: You're already registered for {{jornada}}. To add the other day, do it from its own card.

sedeSection.descripcion: TEA Tenerife Espacio de las Artes will host the academic sessions. Designed by Herzog & de Meuron together with Virgilio Gutiérrez, the building is located in central Santa Cruz de Tenerife, a short walk from MUNA.

participantes.parrafo1: The symposium brings together 25 invited participants from museums, universities, heritage administrations and international organisations.

programa.parrafo: Each speaker will have 10 minutes. Every panel will then leave substantial time for discussion among participants and questions from the audience.

d1-2.descripcion: Institutional participation expected from the Government of the Canary Islands, Cabildo de Tenerife, Organismo Autónomo de Museos y Centros, Museum of Nature and Archaeology, and the Scientific Committee.

d1-4.titulo: Panel I. Unequal collecting and museums: histories and practices of appropriation

d1-6.titulo: Panel II. Cooperation and restitution: policies and frameworks for action

d1-8.titulo: Panel III. International experiences: Europe, Africa and Latin America

d2-1.titulo: Panel IV. The Canary Islands as a case study: displacement, partnerships and expectations of restitution

d2-2.titulo: Panel V. Key trajectories and distinctive debates

d2-4.titulo: Panel VI. Human remains and ethics: science, sensitivity and public responsibility

d2-6.descripcion: Reading of the “Santa Cruz de Tenerife Declaration” and institutional closing.
